title: WHEN KINDNESS FEELS LIKE A TRAP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, 'Take these men to my house, slaughter an animal and prepare a meal; they are to eat with me at noon.' The man did as Joseph told him and took the men to Joseph's house. Now the men were frightened when they were taken to his house. They thought, 'We were brought here because of the silver that was put back into our sacks the first time. He wants to attack us and overpower us and seize us as slaves and take our donkeys.'" - Gen 43:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph, overjoyed to see Benjamin, plans a generous feast: "Take these men to my house... they are to eat with me." It is an act of extraordinary kindness — an invitation to dine at the ruler's own table. Yet the brothers are terrified. Being led to Joseph's house, they imagine the worst: "He wants to attack us and overpower us and seize us as slaves." An invitation to a banquet feels to them like a march to their doom.

Why did they so completely misread this kindness? Because their guilty consciences filled them with dread. Weighed down by their past and the mystery of the returned silver, they could not imagine being treated with grace. They assumed the worst because guilt had taught them to expect punishment.

We can be just like this with God. His invitations of grace can feel, to a fearful and guilty heart, like traps. When God draws us near, offers us mercy, or opens a door of blessing, we may shrink back, suspicious, sure that something bad must be coming. Our guilt whispers that we do not deserve kindness, so we brace ourselves for judgment when God is actually preparing a feast.

Do not let a fearful heart misread God's grace. He does not draw you near to destroy you but to bless you. When God invites you to His table, come — not with dread, but with humble gratitude. The invitation is real, and the kindness is genuine.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I misread God's kindness as a trap because of guilt or fear?
2. When God invites me near, do I come with dread or gratitude?
3. Where do I need to trust that God's grace is genuine?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, do not let my fearful, guilty heart misread Your kindness. When You invite me near, help me to come with gratitude rather than dread, trusting that Your grace toward me is real. Amen.
